_comment: Monster stats, looks and abilities, loaded when the game starts. See DESIGN.md for the roguelike mode.
Enemies: hp and speed (pixels per second) before the wave's hp multiplier and buffs; cost is what the
monster costs to draft and the gold a tower player gets for killing it; damage is the lives it takes
if it gets through (fatal: true takes them all); gap is the seconds before the next spawn.
draft: starter (always draftable), unlock (needs an unlock card), boss (only in a boss level's last
wave), never (only spawned by other monsters).
Look: size, color [r, g, b], sides (0 = circle) or shape, optional inner [shape, radius, color].
Optional mechanics: armor (flat damage blocked per hit, burn excluded), heal_aura [radius, share of
max hp healed per second], split [kind, count] on death, phase [every, for] seconds untargetable,
slow_floor (slows can't push speed below this share; 1 = immune), summon [kind, count, every, optional
[offsets]: where along the path each one lands, in pixels from the summoner, - behind], ward
(seconds: a ward absorbs the next hit whole, burns excluded, slows and burns included, then recharges),
decoy [every, ahead, life]: every `every` seconds an illusion of the monster appears `ahead` pixels
further along the path; one hit pops it, it's worth no gold, takes no lives, and fades after `life` s;
enrage (speed share gained at 0 hp, growing as hp is lost: 1 = twice as fast near death), rebound
[speed share, seconds]: when a slow wears off it sprints that much faster for that long (a new slow ends it),
sabotage [radius, seconds]: when it's killed, towers within radius stop firing for that long (as EMP does),
loot [share, budget]: when it gets through, it steals that share of the tower player's gold (Towers side), or
brings `budget` times its cost back into the monster player's budget (Monsters side), speed_aura
[radius, share]: monsters within radius (not itself) move that share faster (the strongest aura counts).
Abilities, used by the monster player during a wave: target is area (a click on the map, with
radius) or all (every monster). Effects: disable (towers stop firing), range (towers lose `amount` of
their range), haste (monsters gain `amount` speed), heal (`amount` of max hp), shield (monsters take
`amount` less damage). Durations and cooldowns are in seconds of game time.
Budget, for each wave the monster player drafts: the larger of what the generated wave is worth and
share x the value of the defender's comp for that wave. share starts at share_start, grows with every
Monsters level won in the run (by the record tier's share, see rewards), and at the start of each level
moves by pace_per_life for every life the run is behind (up) or ahead of (down) an even pace (the
defender's lives spread evenly over the levels): up by at most pace_max, down by at most pace_min (0:
being ahead never lowers it). starter_picks: unlock
cards offered (one pick-1-of-3 screen each) the first time the Monsters side is played.
upgrade_price: what one rank of a stat upgrade costs, as a share of the current level's budget (the
five waves' budgets added up), times the rank being bought. escort_per_wave: the most escort Basics
(see upgrades) sent with one wave; the rest wait for the next waves. max_lives_per_level: the most
of the defender's lives one Monsters level can take (0: no limit).
Upgrades: bought on the Monsters side with the budget; they last for the rest of the pass and apply to
every monster sent. stat is hp (per_rank: share of max hp), speed (share of speed) or armor (per_rank:
flat damage blocked per hit, added to the type's armor). Every purchase also sends Basics worth its
price as an escort, so the budget spent on it isn't lost to the waves.
Rewards after a win depend on how strong the record beaten was, against par (what the level's generated
waves are worth). Monsters side: the defender's strongest comp in the level / par. Towers side: the
monster record's waves added up (generated waves where there's no record) / par. A ratio under
tiers[side][0] is a weak record, from tiers[side][1] up a strong one, normal in between. Each tier sets
the cards offered (pick 1), whether one of them is a guaranteed rare (if any are left), and how much a
Monsters win grows the budget share for the rest of the run.

emp.name: EMP
emp.desc: Towers in the area stop firing

smoke.name: Smokescreen
smoke.desc: Towers in the area lose 40% range
